title: Check yourself: final references and class dependencies

questions.stem: A field is declared `private final List<String> tags`. Which statement matches what the page says `final` does here?

options.text: The field keeps referring to one list, and that list's contents are frozen
options.says: final fixes only the reference; the page says the object's internal state can still change if it is mutable.

options.text: The field keeps referring to one list, whose contents may still change
options.says: The page says a final object variable cannot point elsewhere, but a mutable object's state can still be modified.

options.text: The field may be pointed at a new list, but only inside instance methods
options.says: A final variable cannot be reassigned anywhere after initialization, in any method.

questions.stem: Two classes each hold a reference to the other and depend on each other's methods. What does the page recommend?

options.text: Make one class extend the other, deepening the hierarchy
options.says: The page's next edge case says to limit inheritance depth, and for a cycle it names interfaces or a redesign.

options.text: Keep the cycle, and make each class's fields public and static
options.says: The page warns against overusing public fields and does not suggest keeping the cycle.

options.text: Break the cycle with an interface, or redesign the structure
options.says: The page's advice on circular dependencies is to use interfaces or redesign the class structure.
